title: Count words until the end of the input

blocks.text: Reading input until it runs out is the textbook `while` loop:
`readLine()` returns `null` at the end of the input, and the input may hold no line at all.
Write `count(BufferedReader reader)` in `Words`. It returns how many words the whole input holds, where words are separated by any run of spaces or tabs:

items:
a blank line holds none: `"a

   
b"` holds `2`;
extra spaces separate nothing more: `"  a   b  "` holds `2`;

cases.says: Every line's words are counted, to the end of the input.

"a

   
b" holds 2 words: a blank line holds none.
"  a   b  " holds 2 words: a run of spaces is one separator.
An empty input holds 0 words: the loop body never runs.

concepts: Reading with while ((line = reader.readLine()) != null) processes every line until the end of the input.
